description: Society and population: from a country or region to cited income, poverty and inequality figures (World Bank PIP, Eurostat EU-SILC, OECD IDD) side by side with definitions, release vintages, PPP rounds and comparability notes, as of a date, over shared Geospatial, entity-identity, subscription and source-acquisition providers; Demographics denominators and Labour series linked by citation when present. Figures are quoted as each source released them; nothing is nowcast, filled, blended or re-harmonised.

profiles.description: Place-centred income, poverty and inequality figures per source, as of a release

vocabulary.vintage: one release of a series with its release and retrieval clocks
vocabulary.PPP round: the PPP base year a poverty line and monetary figures are stated in
vocabulary.welfare concept: income or consumption as the source measures it
vocabulary.comparability_unknown: two vintages with no stated or recorded note

profiles.description: Place-centred social protection expenditure, beneficiaries and coverage per source (Eurostat ESSPROS, OECD SOCX, ILOSTAT SDG 1.3.1), as of a release, side by side and never blended

vocabulary.function: the publisher's own classification: ESSPROS function (spfunc), SOCX policy area or ILO contingency; related across publishers only by review, never re-classified
vocabulary.measure: expenditure, beneficiaries or coverage; never presented as measuring the same thing
vocabulary.COFOG: general-government expenditure by function in economics.public-finance; a third, distinct concept
vocabulary.edition: a World Social Protection Report edition; a restating edition is a new vintage
vocabulary.comparability_unknown: two vintages or rows with no stated or recorded note

exclusions: nowcasting income, poverty or inequality figures
filling years a source did not publish
poverty lines of our own (only the lines a source publishes)
blending PIP, EU-SILC and OECD figures into one series
re-harmonising welfare concepts, equivalence scales or income definitions
deriving indicators (rates, ratios, shares or counts) that no source published
never: set a poverty line of our own
blend or average figures across sources
re-harmonise welfare concepts or equivalence scales
